purpose: Define what a genuinely deep Atlas entry is. A label, description, or snippet is not considered a completed record.
principle: The Atlas is a reference work and relationship graph, not a catalogue of labels.

depth_levels.2: record: structured metadata and some relationships
depth_levels.3: substantive: coherent explanatory article with timeline, structure and evidence
depth_levels.4: deep: substantive article plus primary sources, internal subdivisions, people, places, concepts and dense relationships
depth_levels.5: corpus: deep record plus complete reusable primary texts, stable passages and cross-text navigation

quality_rules: Never mark a metadata-only record as deep.
Never use a generic placeholder as the substance of an entry.
A relationship must point to a real canonical ID or be explicitly marked unresolved.
Historical traditions must preserve internal diversity, timeline and disagreement.
Comparative similarities must be labelled as parallel, analogy, influence, contradiction or unknown rather than silently equated.
Primary text is kept separate from interpretation.
Where a complete text cannot legally be stored, retain provenance, structure, short quotations where permitted and an external source link.
Every important record should be useful without leaving the Atlas, while source links remain available for verification.
required_deep_sections: How it works or is structured
